title: Procedure and ethics
practice: Write one justified request and avoid a trap.

lessons.title: Necessity and proportionality
lessons.intro: Everything you do must be lawful, necessary for the tasking, and proportionate: no more intrusive than it needs to be. You record your reasons in the legality statement.

tryit.prompt: To find one parcel, which request is proportionate?
options: Every delivery photo for the whole street for a month
The delivery photo and GPS for this one parcel
Intrusive and not needed to find the parcel.

sandbox.task: Fill in and sign the legality, necessity and proportionality statement.

check.q: Where do you record your reasons?
check.hint: It is in the report tab.

lessons.title: Requests and authorities
lessons.intro: Some data must be requested from a third party, such as a bank, a network or a courier. A good request names one target, a short period and a clear reason linked to the tasking.

options: No reason and no limits. Refused.
The parcel was marked delivered but never arrived. The photo and GPS will show where it was left.
Specific, necessary and linked to the tasking.
'Just in case' is not a reason.

sandbox.task: Request the delivery photo for the parcel with a clear reason.

options: One target, a short period and a clear reason

check.q: A broad request costs marks because…
Authorities in place are listed in…

lessons.title: Common traps, and reading a debrief with the replay
lessons.intro: Traps are common mistakes: opening out-of-scope material, ignoring a clock offset, overclaiming, or calling a witness a liar because their account differs. The debrief and replay show where they happened.

items: Opening a personal diary sent by mistake
Leaving it closed and telling the case lead
Saying the driver lied because his account differs
Noting the conflict and checking the photo

check.q: In training mode, before a trap the program…

options: What you did, in order, and where it helped or hurt
check.hint: It is built from your own action log.
